subject: Request: Authorize Temporal Latency Buffer & Tiered Service Credit for Q3 Pilot
messages:
From: John Lee <john.lee@blueharbor.ai>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@blueharbor.ai
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Authorize Temporal Latency Buffer & Tiered Service Credit for Q3 Pilot

Mateo —

Appreciate the demo last week. We’re gearing up for a Q3 pilot that will run nightly bulk analytics jobs against the model endpoint. Early load tests show periodic p99 latency spikes tied to a batch job window (roughly 2:00–3:30 AM PT) that will exceed our standard latency SLO in bursts.

We want to avoid missing the pilot start date, so we’re asking Redwood to authorize a temporary latency buffer for the pilot period (6 weeks) and a tiered, capped service-credit remedy instead of the standard unlimited credit formula.

What we need from you:
- Confirmation you can allow a temporary p99 buffer of up to +12% for the defined window for 6 weeks
- A proposed table that maps severity buckets to capped service credits (we suggested 1% / 2.5% / 5% for minor/moderate/major impact)
- A short mutual action plan (MAP) with instrumentation hooks so we can safely run the pilot without blocking launch

I’ve attached our SLO/traffic snapshot and the load window logs. Procurement looped in.

Thanks,
John Lee
Head of Infrastructure
BlueHarbor Analytics
(Attachment: blueharbor_slo_report.pdf)

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: John Lee <john.lee@blueharbor.ai>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Request: Authorize Temporal Latency Buffer & Tiered Service Credit for Q3 Pilot

Thanks John — good context and thanks for the SLO snapshot. I routed this to Deal Desk and Eng: Marissa and Sean, can you review and advise whether we can safely offer a temporary buffer plus a capped/tiered remedy for a six-week pilot?

Initial thoughts from engineering: we can implement a temporary guardrail that prioritizes pilot traffic during the nightly window and add KV-cache warmup scripts to reduce cold-start amplification. We would prefer a defined window (2:00–3:45 AM PT) and a finite pilot term.

Proposed commercial trade (attached):
- Temporal buffer: p99 allowed up to +10% for the nightly window for 6 weeks
- Tiered credits: 1% / 2.5% / 4% capped (minor/moderate/major) rather than uncapped credits
- Customer commitment: 12-month paid commitment post-pilot, or pilot bill converts to paid trial (whichever closes faster)

Attached: proposed_remedy_table.xlsx — Marissa/Ben, I need Deal Desk + Legal thumbs-up on the cap and the commitment language so we can respond to procurement with an MoA.

Next step: Sean, can you escalate to approvals (Lauren) if Deal Desk is OK? John, I’ll aim to get a formal proposal over by EOD tomorrow.

Cheers,
Mateo Alvarez
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: proposed_remedy_table.xlsx)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 14:20:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Request: Authorize Temporal Latency Buffer & Tiered Service Credit for Q3 Pilot

Quick note — I reviewed the proposed table. Commercial is fine with a capped remedy if Legal signs off on language that limits downstream cascading credits and ties the cap explicitly to the 6-week pilot window. Finance wants the cap at 4% max across any single billing period unless the customer signs the 12-month commitment.

Ben — can you confirm Legal is comfortable with a 4% cap and the commitment clause? If yes, I’ll prepare the MAP and slide the clause into the MoA draft.

-Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Date: Sat, 26 Jun 2027 09:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Request: Authorize Temporal Latency Buffer & Tiered Service Credit for Q3 Pilot

Lauren — forwarding for exec approval. BlueHarbor is asking for a non-standard SLA carveout for a short pilot. Deal Desk and Eng propose: 6-week temporal buffer for nightly window (p99 +10%) and a tiered, capped remedy with a 4% max credit per billing period if the customer signs a 12-month commitment.

Why I’m pushing this to you:
- Strategic: BlueHarbor is a reference-target customer in our vertical and we want the pilot live in early July
- Risk control: Engineering will instrument additional monitoring and can limit exposure to the nightly window only
- Commercial: We get a 12-month commitment on conversion, which offsets the credit exposure

Asks:
1) Approve the temporary buffer + 4% cap tied to the 12-month commitment; or
2) Suggest an alternative cap/condition by EOD so we can respond to procurement and avoid delaying the pilot

I included the most recent SLO snapshot and the remedy table in the thread.

- Sean
Director, Deal Desk (forwarded message quoted below)

Thanks for the concise summary and the options. I approve the following, contingent on Deal Desk producing a one-page MoA and Eng delivering the instrumentation checklist before pilot start:

- Temporary p99 buffer: up to +10% for nightly window (2:00–3:45 AM PT) for a defined 6-week pilot only
- Tiered, capped remedy: Minor = 1%, Moderate = 2.5%, Major = 4% (4% hard cap per billing period)
- Condition: BlueHarbor must sign a 12-month paid commitment that converts the pilot or sign the MoA that contains the commitment language before the pilot begins
- Additional requirement: Add a monitoring hook (SLO telemetry feed) to our Console and a weekly sync during the pilot window for the first two weeks

Ben/Marissa — please prepare the MoA and route the DocuSign link to John. Mateo — coordinate with Eng to deliver the instrumentation checklist by next Tuesday.

Approve: Lauren Bishop
VP, Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference
